tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED, and the cause is a supplier that CANNOT answer — not the model, and not the tool.

SURFACED 5/5 but called 0/5, which is a different finding from the last three batches: this tool WAS advertised. In the measured turn the model made ZERO tool calls and said "Since I have no record of the 'Obsidian Trench' in your project's memory or manuscript, I cannot forget a fact that isn't currently stored".

🔴 IT WAS RIGHT, AND THE STORE PROVES BOTH HALVES. The seed stored TWO facts — the run's own snapshot reads neo4j.Fact.project = 2 before and after — so the facts exist. But a direct probe of the supplier shows why turn 1 found nothing:
    memory_search(query='Obsidian Trench') -> {"hits": [], "total": 0,
                                               "degraded": {"semantic": "not_indexed"},
                                               "note": "this project has no indexed memory yet"}
A fact stored by memory_remember is NOT findable by memory_search until the project is indexed. memory_forget's own description says 'Only use a fact_id you have seen in an earlier tool result' — so on an unindexed project its single supplier returns nothing and the tool is unreachable BY DESIGN, however well the model behaves.

NAMING IT: D-STORED-BUT-UNFINDABLE-UNTIL-INDEXED. It is the exact shape found one batch earlier in the graph subsystem — D-EDGELESS-NODE-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-GRAPH-READ, where kg_add_nodes says 'node ready' and kg_graph_query reports zero nodes. Two independent subsystems, one pattern: a write tool confirms it stored something and the only read that would surface it returns nothing, so the model tells the author their own content is not there. In both cases the model's sentence was TRUE and the false absence belonged to the platform.
